messages:
sara-support: Customer on private/VPC reporting intermittent 502s when routing via their enterprise proxy. App talks to our Private endpoint over HTTP CONNECT, and they see TLS handshake failures / cert mismatch (proxy serving its own cert). They say it works from other networks. Can SRE advise?

devin-sre: Can you paste the exact curl/command they're using and a short repro? most likely transparent proxy doing TLS interception instead of tunneling.

sara-support: Customer repro steps (from them):
- `curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 https://private.redwood.internal/v1/generate`
- response: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and `SSL: certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain`
- they ran `openssl s_client -connect corp-proxy:8080 -servername private.redwood.internal` and got the proxy cert, CN=corp-proxy.local

devin-sre: That matches TLS inspection. With HTTP CONNECT we expect the proxy to pipe a raw TCP tunnel for port 443. If the proxy terminates TLS you will see their cert. Ask them to configure the proxy to allow CONNECT passthrough for our hostnames or disable MITM for those endpoints.

ingrid-platops: Quick checklist to send the customer:
1) Confirm the proxy is using explicit intercept/SSL inspection. (they already saw proxy cert)
2) Recommend `CONNECT` tunneling for `private.redwood.internal:443` instead of SSL bump.
3) If using Squid/BlueCoat/F5, give example rules to splice/tunneled mode.
4) Temp workaround: run the request from a network that doesn't inspect TLS or use IP-based egress that bypasses proxy.

devin-sre: Example Squid snippet to splice (give to their proxy admin):
```
# allow passthrough for our private endpoint
acl redwood_hosts dstdomain .private.redwood.internal
acl SSL_ports port 443
ssl_bump splice redwood_hosts
ssl_bump none all
```
Note: exact config depends on Squid version. For BlueCoat look for "SSL interception bypass" rules.

ops-bot: [log] 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z upstream_error id=svc-private-03 code=502 msg="tls handshake failed: remote_cert=corp-proxy.local"

sara-support: @devin-sre customer proxy team says they "can't disable inspection globally" but can add exceptions. What minimum host patterns should they allow?

devin-sre: Allowlist `private.redwood.internal` and any pinned IP ranges we gave them. If they rely on SNI allowlist, ensure SNI is preserved (no SNI rewrite). If their proxy rewrites Host/SNI, they need passthrough. Also check ALPN — proxy must not terminate TLS to change ALPN.

ingrid-platops: If they cannot change proxy rules quickly, a short-term workaround: use a dedicated egress (VPN or NAT) that bypasses corp proxy, or spin up an internal reverse-proxy that performs TLS passthrough to our endpoint (but that still requires their org to allow outbound 443 to our IPs).

sara-support: Customer asked for a minimal test they can run. Send this: 
```
# from a machine behind the proxy:
openssl s_client -connect corp-proxy:8080 -servername private.redwood.internal -verify_return_error
# If you see corp-proxy cert instead of our CA chain, proxy is terminating TLS
```

devin-sre: Also ask them to capture a short tcpdump showing the CONNECT exchange and the TLS ClientHello SNI if visible, or provide proxy logs showing CONNECT method was issued vs intercepted. Example `tcpdump -w capture.pcap host corp-proxy and port 443` and share pcap.

ingrid-platops: We should also check our side: confirm we aren't redirecting to a different hostname that triggers proxy policy. Confirmed: private endpoint serves cert for `private.redwood.internal` (ok).

ops-bot: [note] requested pcap upload link created: https://files.redwood.internal/upload/req-9876

sara-support: Customer proxy admin applied a passthrough rule for `private.redwood.internal` and retested. They report: "requests succeed, no 502, tls chain shows our cert" :tada:

devin-sre: Great — will follow up in 24h to confirm stability. Recommend they keep allowlist for our hostnames and IP ranges in their change control.

sara-support: Closing once customer confirms in prod. Thanks all for the quick triage :thumbsup:
